message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles by visiting one of the following resources:

| Source | What it shows | How to use |
|--------|---------------|------------|
| **AirNow** (airnow.gov) | Current AQI, pollutant levels (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), forecast | Search “Los Angeles” or enter the ZIP code. |
| **EPA Air Quality Index** (aqicn.org) | Live AQI map, historical data, health advice | Select “Los Angeles” on the map. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | News‑style updates, alerts | Look for “air quality” or “AQI” in the search bar. |
| **Weather apps** (Weather.com, AccuWeather, Weather Underground) | AQI integrated into weather forecasts | Open the app, type “Los Angeles,” and scroll to the AQI section. |

**Quick tip:** If you’re planning outdoor activities, check the AQI at least 24 hours before. An AQI of 0–50 is “Good,” 51–100 “Moderate,” 101–150 “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups,” 151–200 “Unhealthy,” 201–300 “Very Unhealthy,” and 301+ “Hazardous.”
